chapters.title: Students who can explain their own learning
chapters.lede: Student Learning is the student-facing reflection and ownership layer of the Academic Quality Ecosystem. It answers one question: **how does the student see, reflect on, and communicate their learning?**

blocks.lead: Two connected practices: a **student portfolio** of selected learning evidence from Grade 7 to Grade 12, and **Student-Led Conferences** where the student presents that evidence to their parents.
points: **Select evidence; do not collect everything** — about 1–2 purposeful pieces per subject per semester.
Use **authentic work already done** in class — no portfolio-only assignments.
The portfolio is **formative and non-graded** — it never creates a second score or a second gradebook.
Two portfolio-led review / SLC cycles a year, **one in each semester**, on dates the school sets.

blocks.title: The student learning cycle
blocks.intro: A strong portfolio entry makes the learning process visible.

steps.title: Evidence
steps.text: A piece of real work that shows learning.

steps.title: Reflection
steps.text: What did I learn? What was difficult?

steps.title: Feedback response
steps.text: What feedback did I get, and what did I change?

steps.title: Follow-up
steps.text: Checked at the next homeroom or advisor check-in.

check: Evidence → Reflection → Feedback Response → Goal → Follow-up

chapters.title: What goes in, and how independence grows
chapters.lede: The portfolio shows progress over time, not the volume of work completed.

chapters.title: The student is the presenter
chapters.lede: The student leads, the teacher facilitates, the parents listen and support. Sensitive, disciplinary, safeguarding or serious academic concerns are discussed separately and privately.

blocks.title: A suggested student flow

steps.title: Welcome
steps.text: “I will show you examples of my learning and explain my progress and next goals.”

steps.title: A strength
steps.text: “This work shows… I am proud of it because…”

steps.title: A challenge
steps.text: “This was difficult because… I changed or improved…”

steps.title: Progress
steps.text: “At the beginning I… Now I can…”

steps.title: Goal & questions
steps.text: “My next goal is…” — then the parents ask questions.

source.at: A. Student Guide — Suggested Student Flow

check: The student is the main presenter. The teacher facilitates.

blocks.title: For the teacher in the room
do: Let the student lead; prompt only when they get stuck.
Protect the student's dignity and the learning focus.
Help confirm the final goal and first action.
dont: Taking over or turning it into a teacher report.
Comparing the student with siblings or classmates.
check: comparing the student with siblings or classmates
correcting every language error

chapters.title: Keep it light, keep it formative
chapters.lede: The layer should simplify the learning-evidence trail — not create a separate reporting bureaucracy.

blocks.title: Protected boundaries
do: One approved platform or format, and a manageable evidence plan.
Student and teacher orientation, with short teacher calibration.
A designated Portfolio Coordinator and regular check-ins.
Privacy, access, retention, export and backup arrangements.
dont: Turn the portfolio into a second assessment system.
Expose confidential assessment information outside authorised systems.
Rank schools or students by upload counts.
check: Do not turn the portfolio into a second assessment system
Do not rank schools or students by upload counts

blocks.title: How School Appraisal uses it
blocks.text: School Appraisal **may sample** portfolio and SLC evidence — especially for Domain 2 — to understand reflection, feedback use and goal-setting. It looks at **quality and authenticity, not upload counts**, and the portfolio **creates no separate appraisal score**.

blocks.text: Student portfolios are kept in the school's **approved format or platform**. Grades 7–12 follow this network model; Early Years and Primary follow the Primary Director's documents.
